title: Open & Convert Esri LPK, MPK and GDB Files Online: No ArcGIS Needed | GeoUnpack
description: Free online tool to open .lpk, .lpkx, .mpk, .mpkx and zipped .gdb files and convert them to Shapefile, GeoJSON, KML, CSV or GeoPackage. Runs in your browser; files are never uploaded.
lead: Drop an Esri package or a zipped file geodatabase below. GeoUnpack lists every layer, previews it on a map, and exports it to the format you need. All inside your browser.
steps: Drop your .lpk, .lpkx, .mpk, .mpkx or zipped .gdb file into the box.
Check the layers you want. Click Preview to see a layer on the map.
Pick an output format and click Convert & download.
faq: Is my file uploaded to a server?
No. GeoUnpack runs the open-source GDAL and 7-Zip libraries inside your browser using WebAssembly. Your file never leaves your computer.
Which files can I open?

ArcGIS layer packages (.lpk, .lpkx), map packages (.mpk, .mpkx) and file geodatabases (.gdb folders compressed as .zip). Vector layers and attribute tables are supported. Raster, tile and scene packages are not supported yet.
Do I need ArcGIS or QGIS?
No. You only need a modern browser such as Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer.
Is there a size limit?
Files up to 150 MB are supported for now, because everything runs in your browser's memory.
subtitle: Open LPK, MPK and GDB files without ArcGIS. Preview the layers and convert them to Shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, KML or CSV.

title: LPK to Shapefile Converter: Convert ArcGIS Layer Package to SHP Online | GeoUnpack
description: Convert .lpk and .lpkx layer packages to Shapefile (.shp) online without ArcGIS. Free, runs in your browser, files are never uploaded.
lead: An .lpk file is a compressed package that holds a layer's data (usually a file geodatabase) and its styling. GeoUnpack unpacks it and exports the data as a zipped Shapefile you can open in QGIS, AutoCAD Map 3D, Global Mapper or any GIS.
steps: Drop the .lpk or .lpkx file into the box.
Select the layer (Preview shows it on a map).
Keep 'SHP (Shapefile)' selected and click Convert & download.
faq: Can I just rename the .lpk to .zip?
Often yes. An .lpk is a 7-Zip archive. You can extract it with 7-Zip and load the .gdb folder in QGIS. GeoUnpack does the same in one step, and also converts the data if you don't have QGIS.
Will the symbology be kept?
No. Shapefiles store geometry and attributes only. Colors, labels and symbols from the .lyr/.lyrx file are not converted.
Why are some field names shortened?
The Shapefile format limits field names to 10 characters and can truncate very large numbers. If exact values matter, export to GeoPackage or GeoJSON instead.
subtitle: Convert ArcGIS layer packages (.lpk, .lpkx) to Shapefile. No ArcGIS needed.

title: LPK to KML Converter: Open ArcGIS Layer Packages in Google Earth | GeoUnpack
description: Turn an ArcGIS .lpk or .lpkx layer package into a KML file you can open in Google Earth. Free online, no ArcGIS, no upload.
lead: Got an .lpk but only have Google Earth? GeoUnpack extracts the layer, reprojects it to WGS84 and writes a KML file Google Earth can open.
steps: Drop the .lpk or .lpkx file into the box.
Select the layer you want.
Choose 'KML (Google Earth)' and click Convert & download, then open the file in Google Earth.
faq: Will it line up correctly in Google Earth?
Yes. KML must use WGS84 longitude/latitude, so GeoUnpack reprojects the data automatically from the package's coordinate system.
Does KML keep the attributes?
Yes, attributes are stored as extended data and show in the feature balloon in Google Earth.
subtitle: Convert ArcGIS layer packages to KML and open them in Google Earth.

title: LPK to GeoJSON Converter Online: Free, No Upload | GeoUnpack
description: Convert ArcGIS .lpk and .lpkx layer packages to GeoJSON for web maps (Leaflet, Mapbox, deck.gl). Free and private: runs in your browser.
lead: GeoJSON is the easiest format for web maps and scripts. GeoUnpack converts the layer inside your .lpk to GeoJSON in WGS84 with six-decimal precision.
steps: Drop the .lpk or .lpkx file into the box.
Select one or more layers.
Choose 'GeoJSON' and click Convert & download.
faq: What coordinate system does the GeoJSON use?
WGS84 (EPSG:4326), as required by the GeoJSON specification.
My GeoJSON is very large. Why?
GeoJSON is plain text and detailed polygons produce big files. For large layers, GeoPackage is more compact.
subtitle: Convert ArcGIS layer packages to GeoJSON (WGS84) for web maps and scripts.

faq: What is an .lpk file?
An ArcGIS layer package. It bundles a layer's styling (.lyr) with a copy of its data, usually in a file geodatabase, compressed into a single file for sharing.
How do I open an .lpk in QGIS?
Extract it with 7-Zip, open the 'v10' or 'v108' folder and drag the .gdb folder into QGIS. Or convert it to Shapefile or GeoPackage here.

title: How to Open an LPK File Without ArcGIS (3 Ways) | GeoUnpack
h1: Open an LPK File Without ArcGIS
description: Three ways to open an ArcGIS .lpk layer package without ArcGIS: an online converter, 7-Zip + QGIS, or GDAL's ogr2ogr. Step-by-step.
lead: You don't need an ArcGIS licence to get the data out of an .lpk. Use the tool below, or follow one of the free manual methods further down.
steps: Easiest: drop the .lpk below and export to Shapefile, GeoPackage or KML.
With QGIS: extract the .lpk with 7-Zip, then drag the .gdb folder from the 'v10'/'v108' subfolder into QGIS.
With GDAL: extract it, then run ogr2ogr -f GPKG out.gpkg path/to/data.gdb.
faq: Which method should I use?
If you already have QGIS, method 2 is free and keeps everything local. If you don't want to install anything, use the online tool. It also runs locally in your browser.
Can I edit the data?
Once exported to Shapefile or GeoPackage you can edit it in any GIS. The original .lpk is not changed.
subtitle: Use the converter below, or follow one of the free manual methods further down.

.lpk comes from ArcMap, .lpkx from ArcGIS Pro. Both are 7-Zip archives containing the layer data.
